The buggy method is `org.jfree.chart.axis.Axis.drawLabel(java.lang.String, java.awt.Graphics2D, java.awt.geom.Rectangle2D, java.awt.geom.Rectangle2D, org.jfree.chart.util.RectangleEdge, org.jfree.chart.axis.AxisState, org.jfree.chart.plot.PlotRenderingInfo)`.

Why this is the best diagnosis:
- The failures are broad but tightly clustered around category-chart drawing with `null` info.
- `JFreeChart.draw(...)` passes `null` plot info when the caller supplies `null` chart info.
- `CategoryPlot.draw(...)` explicitly supports that case by creating a temporary `new PlotRenderingInfo(null)` so later code can still use plot geometry.
- `CategoryAxis.drawCategoryLabels(...)` is careful: it checks both `plotState != null` and `plotState.getOwner() != null` before touching entities.
- `Axis.drawLabel(...)` is not careful enough. At lines 1190-1193 it does:

```java
if (plotState != null && hotspot != null) {
    ChartRenderingInfo owner = plotState.getOwner();
    EntityCollection entities = owner.getEntityCollection();
    ...
}
```

In the null-info path, `plotState` is non-null but `plotState.getOwner()` is null, so `owner.getEntityCollection()` throws a `NullPointerException`.

That matches the failure pattern:
- many category chart types fail,
- renderer-specific tests fail even though the underlying issue is shared,
- serialization tests fail when they eventually redraw the same plot,
- tests named `testDrawWithNullInfo()` are exactly exercising this path.

The fix should be to guard `owner` before dereferencing it in `Axis.drawLabel(...)`, consistent with the existing null-safe pattern already used in `CategoryAxis.drawCategoryLabels(...)`.
